title: Uniqueness of the absolute value on an algebraic extension of a complete nonarchimedean field
statement: Let $K$ be a field complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|_K$, and let $L/K$ be an algebraic field extension, meaning that each element of $L$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial in $K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Let $u,v:L\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ be absolute values (each is multiplicative, vanishes exactly at $0$, and satisfies the triangle inequality). Assume $u(a)=v(a)=|a|_K$ for every $a\in K$, using the inclusion $K\hookrightarrow L$. Then $u(x)=v(x)$ for every $x\in L$. No finite-degree assumption on $L/K$ is imposed.

from.place: det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Smooth-curve abelian level rigidification. Geometric stabilizer input for the smooth full-level cover; restrict to geometric curves before passing to families. Auxiliary input: Prime-to-characteristic level rigidity for polarized abelian varieties. Supporting input in the level-rigidity proof: Chapter I, Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; polarization convention in I §11, printed p.53. Supporting fact for Proposition 14.4(a): Chapter I §14, printed p.61 (Rosati formula and involution), Theorem 14.3, printed p.62 (positive trace form); §11 p.53 (polarization isogeny); Proposition 10.20, printed pp.50–52 (trace on Tate modules). Supporting input: Chapter I, Theorem 10.9 and Remark 10.11, pp.46–48; Proposition 10.20 and proof, pp.50–52. Rational extension by clearing denominators as in Remark 10.11. Supporting input in the present split: Chapter I, Lemma 10.21 and its proof, printed p.51. Supporting identity in Milne I Lemma 10.21, p.51: the two displayed root-product formulas for the minimum polynomial of alpha. The assertion that automorphisms preserve valuations: uniqueness of extension to the algebraic closure.
